title: Incentives, Remuneration and Performance Management
summary: How sales targets, remuneration and performance management shape behaviour, and how supervisors assess whether incentive schemes encourage poor outcomes or misconduct.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How sales targets, remuneration and performance management shape behaviour, and how supervisors assess whether incentive schemes encourage poor outcomes or misconduct.
Learning Objectives: Explain how incentives drive front-line and management behaviour
Evaluate the design and controls of incentive and remuneration schemes
Identify incentive structures linked to poor outcomes and mis-selling
Syllabus: Variable pay, sales targets and balanced scorecards
Non-financial incentives: promotion, recognition and pressure
Controls: deferral, malus, clawback and quality gateways
Intended Audience: Conduct and consumer protection supervisors, including those supervising retail-facing firms
Prudential and governance supervisors seeking to assess culture and its link to risk
Policy, data and enforcement staff working on conduct risk and customer outcomes
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of conduct or consumer protection supervision is helpful. No background in economics or behavioural science is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
FSB, Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture (2014)
Group of Thirty, Banking Conduct and Culture: A Call for Sustained and Comprehensive Reform (2015)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
